newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline prices end mixed, outlook divided.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline prices end mixed, outlook divided.

text.p: NWE gasoline ended mixed on Tuesday with premium unleaded barges falling about $3 and cargoes gaining $3, traders said.
Price forecasts were equally divided ahead of key American Petroleum Institute data due out later today, which were expected to show a one-million-barrel rise in U.S. gasoline stocks for last week.
Continued buying ahead of the U.K. budget on November 26 was expected to support cargo prices, traders said, after a Scandinavian producer again was a noted buyer in the barge market today.
In addition, a 10,000-tonne Eurograde cargo traded at $229.50 cif into the Thames, confirming traders' beliefs that barges were being bought up to load onto cargoes and be shipped to the U.K.
And traders said any further gains in NYMEX gasoline fuelled by this week's inventory data could attract further barrels from Northwest Europe.
"Today is a key day. The market is struggling to establish a clear direction," said one trader at a central European refinery.
"I think the gasoline arb to the U.S. is becoming more and more attractive and if New York rallies it will put the fire under the market in Europe," he said.
Stitching Euroilstock said on Tuesday that European Union gasoline stocks (excluding Sweden) fell 3.74 million barrels, or 2.4 percent, in October to 153 million.
But other traders warned that any lightening up in barge demand and further losses in Brent crude could quickly drag gasoline prices lower.
Demand for regular unleaded also appears thin with its discount to premium unleaded widening from $10 late last week to $12 to $14, traders said.
"The regular market is very thin in comparison to Eurograde...There is no demand," a trader said.
He also remarked that the arbitrage to the U.S. was "a shaky animal" and it was not certain if more barrels would cross the Atlantic, following last week's fixture of at least 100,000 tonnes.
Regular unleaded last traded at $209.25 fob ARA after earlier trades at $209 and $210.50.
Unleaded premium traded late at $222 Amsterdam-Rotterdam, down $3.
Premium unleaded cargoes were up $3 at $229 cif.
